files.description: Local HTTP service with health, version, notes and metrics endpoints backed by disposable SQLite data.
HTTP, readiness, persistence, backup and simulated release-restart assertions.
Multi-stage container build that runs service tests and uses a non-root runtime.
Limits the container build context to the required app, tests and Dockerfile.
Setup, exact commands, expected results, cleanup and verification limits.
Three Kubernetes projects with observable outcomes, review criteria and reference approaches.
Offline checks for manifest namespaces, selectors, ports and selected security properties.
Guarded PowerShell helper for local namespace bootstrap, server dry-run, rollout and cleanup.
Dedicated notebook-lab namespace with a training marker and restricted Pod Security policy.
Baseline application Deployment, Service, configuration and service account.
Optional ingress policy; requires a network plugin that actually enforces NetworkPolicy.
Optional read-only Pod/log viewer account, Role and RoleBinding.
Synthetic demonstration Secret containing no real credential.
Optional CPU autoscaler; requires a working resource metrics API.
Optional budget for eligible voluntary Pod evictions.
Bounded in-cluster Job that checks the application through its Service.
Optional volume claim and writer Pod for a local persistence experiment.
Seven offline command-guard tests using a fake kubectl function; no cluster access.

tasks.title: Object and reconciliation notebook
tasks.goal: Explain and optionally run the dedicated local workload without touching a shared cluster.
steps: Extract all listed flat files together into a new practice folder.
Read README.md and the workbook before any optional Docker/cluster command.
Run offline checks and record actual runtime/results.
Run the7 service and4 offline manifest-contract checks.
Draw API→Deployment→ReplicaSet→Pod and Service→EndpointSlices.
Compare labels,selectors,ports and config lifecycle.

Capture desired/current/available counts and local health/version results.
Compare the packet against the stage rubric; separate executed checks from reviewed or planned work.
